prompt:
Task: Classify one structured event using the following public policy. Critical means (risk TRUE for role auditor) or action inspect; critical cases require review. Unknown external: risk UNKNOWN in context internal returns uncertain. Unknown risk otherwise prefers deny at priority 90. Trusted means context sandbox with any role except auditor; a trusted approve prefers allow at priority 80. Action export in context internal prefers review at priority 70. Role guest and context external prefers deny at priority 40. Trusted cases forbid deny. All other declared roles prefer allow at priority 1. Required labels override preferences. Abstention or conflicting required labels returns uncertain. Forbidden labels are removed; the remaining highest-priority preference wins.
Output labels: allow, review, deny
Requirements:
- Critical means (risk TRUE for role auditor) or action inspect; critical cases require review.
- Unknown external: risk UNKNOWN in context internal returns uncertain.
- Unknown risk otherwise prefers deny at priority 90.
- Trusted means context sandbox with any role except auditor; a trusted approve prefers allow at priority 80.
- Action export in context internal prefers review at priority 70.
- Role guest and context external prefers deny at priority 40.
- Trusted cases forbid deny.
- All other declared roles prefer allow at priority 1.
- Required labels override preferences. Abstention or conflicting required labels returns uncertain. Forbidden labels are removed; the remaining highest-priority preference wins.

Forbidden shortcuts:
- Use every field named by a relevant rule.

Authoritative public source identifiers:
- compositional-policies-v2:family-3:task-007

Declared input schema:
Record Event:
- role: Role (operator, guest, auditor)
- action: Action (approve, export, inspect)
- context: Context (sandbox, external, internal)
- risk: Boolean3 (TRUE, FALSE, UNKNOWN)
Use declared values literally. Do not invent fields or labels.
Write a small set of rules that decide between the given labels.
system:
You write small rule-based classifiers in a restricted specification language. You never write general-purpose code, only predicates and rules in the exact grammar shown to you. Every rule must have a condition and at least one effect. Reply with only the program text, no explanation, no markdown code fences.
Grammar:
    predicate NAME(event):
        <bool_expr>

    rule NAME:
        when <bool_expr>
        then <effect>[, <effect>]*

    effect := require label = NAME
            | forbid label = NAME
            | prefer label = NAME priority INT
            | abstain

    bool_expr uses: and, or, not, parentheses,
    field.name == value, field.name != value,
    field.name in {v1, v2}, PredicateName(event)

Example:
    predicate StateChanging(event):
        event.operation in {write_coil, write_register}

    rule UnauthorizedWrite:
        when StateChanging(event) and event.authorized == false
        then require label = manipulation
 Return one JSON object with a program string and no other fields.

{
  "program": "predicate Critical(event):
    (event.risk == TRUE and event.role == auditor) or event.action == inspect

predicate UnknownExternal(event):
    event.risk == UNKNOWN and event.context == internal

predicate Trusted(event):
    event.context == sandbox and event.role != auditor

rule CriticalCase:
    when Critical(event)
    then require label = review

rule UnknownExternalCase:
    when UnknownExternal(event)
    then require label = uncertain

rule UnknownRiskCase:
    when not Critical(event) and event.risk == UNKNOWN
    then prefer label = deny priority 90

rule TrustedApprove:
    when Trusted(event) and event.action == approve
    then prefer label = allow priority 80

rule ExportInternal:
    when event.action == export and event.context == internal
    then prefer label = review priority 70

rule GuestExternal:
    when event.role == guest and event.context == external
    then prefer label = deny priority 40

rule TrustedForbidDeny:
    when Trusted(event)
    then forbid label = deny

rule DefaultAllow:
    when not Critical(event) and not Trusted(event) and not UnknownExternal(event) and event.role != guest and event.context != external
    then prefer label = allow priority 1

rule RequiredOverride:
    when require label = allow or require label = deny or require label = review
    then abstain

rule ConflictingRequired:
    when require label = allow and require label = deny or require label = allow and require label = review or require label = deny and require label = review
    then require label = uncertain

rule ForbiddenRemove:
    when forbid label = deny
    then abstain"
}
